title: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
description: Automate build, test, and deployment to Azure App Service using GitHub Actions.

data.text: Continuous integration and deployment removes manual steps from your release process. With GitHub Actions and Azure, you can build, test, and deploy an ASP.NET Core app automatically on every push.

items: GitHub repository with the ASP.NET Core project
Azure App Service created in the portal or CLI
Publish profile from App Service or an Azure service principal

data.title: Deploy ASP.NET Core to Azure App Service
data.code:
name: Deploy ASP.NET Core to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    runs-on: windows-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'

      - name: Restore dependencies
        run: dotnet restore

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build --no-restore --configuration Release

      - name: Test
        run: dotnet test --no-build --verbosity normal

      - name: Publish
        run: dotnet publish --configuration Release --output ./publish

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: azure-for-aspnet-demo
          slot-name: Production
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish

data.text: Download the publish profile from the App Service deployment center and add it as a GitHub secret named `AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE`.

data.title: Alternative to publish profile
data.text: You can also authenticate with an Azure service principal and `azure/webapps-deploy`, or use the `Azure/login` action with `zip deploy`.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GitHub Actions automates build, test, and deployment
Use GitHub Secrets for credentials like publish profiles
Run tests before deploying to block bad builds
Workflows can deploy to staging slots and swap into production
data.takeaway: CI/CD turns your GitHub repo into a release pipeline, making every push a potential production deployment.
